What @madda/app is and how it compares to all-in-one starters.

**@madda/app** is the official CLI of the [madda](https://www.npmjs.com/org/madda) org. It scaffolds [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) projects with an opinionated **madda stack** — focused on type-safety, developer experience, and conventions that scale. Inspired by the flow of [create-t3-app](https://create.t3.gg/), built for the madda ecosystem. ## Not a kitchen-sink template We are **not** shipping every library you might ever need. The CLI composes **features** you select: - **Tailwind CSS** — optional styling - **ESLint + Prettier** — optional lint/format - **Drizzle ORM** — optional (`postgres` local or `neon`) - **Better Auth** — only when a database is selected - **Events + firewall** — optional rate-limit module when auth + DB are enabled You get a real codebase you can grow — not a framework you fight against. ## What you get out of the box
Layer Default / optional
Framework Next.js (App Router)
Language TypeScript
Env validation @t3-oss/env-nextjs + Zod
Styling Tailwind (optional)
ORM Drizzle (optional)
Auth Better Auth (optional, requires DB)
Logging Pino + optional Axiom transport

Argument / flag Description
[dir] Project directory name (default: my-app)
--default Skip prompts; use the default stack
--no-git Do not run git init

## Examples ```bash # Current directory pnpm create @madda/app . -- --default # No git, no install (CI) pnpm create @madda/app my-app -- --default --noGit --noInstall ``` ## Default stack (`--default`) - Tailwind CSS - ESLint + Prettier - Drizzle + local Postgres - Better Auth - **No** auth events / firewall module For the interactive flow (conditional auth & events prompts), see [Interactive flow](/docs/cli/interactive/).
What the CLI asks when stdin is a TTY.

When you run without `--default` in a terminal, the CLI walks through: 1. **Project name** 2. **Tailwind CSS?** 3. **ESLint + Prettier?** 4. **Database (Drizzle)?** — None · PostgreSQL (Docker) · Neon 5. **Better Auth?** — only if a database was chosen 6. **Include events?** — only if Better Auth + database (firewall / rate-limit) 7. **Initialize git?** 8. **Run install?** ## Rules that matter
Choice Effect
No database Auth and events are not offered
Auth without events Standard Better Auth + Drizzle schema
Auth + events Adds events table, repositories, SQL scripts, db:sql scripts
Non-interactive environments (CI without TTY) get a **minimal** stack unless you pass `--default`.

## Scripts (when Drizzle is enabled) ```bash pnpm db:push # drizzle-kit push pnpm db:studio # Drizzle Studio pnpm db:generate # generate migrations pnpm db:migrate # run migrations ``` ## Schema layout - **Auth only** — `src/server/db/schema/auth.ts` + index - **Auth + events** — adds `events.ts` and exports both from `schema/index.ts` - **No auth** — example `posts` schema for learning Drizzle ## SQL scripts (events module) When events are enabled: ```bash pnpm db:sql # apply all .sql in drizzle/sql/ pnpm db:sql:firewall # apply firewall_create_user.sql only ``` Uses `scripts/apply-sql.ts` with `DATABASE_URL` or `DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE`.
Optional sign-up rate limiting and audit events.

Enable **“Include events?”** in the CLI when you have **Better Auth + Drizzle**. ## What gets added
Path Purpose
src/server/db/schema/events.ts events table
src/repositories/ UserRepository, EventRepository
src/server/db/firewall/create-user.ts Calls SQL function + blocks abusive IPs
drizzle/sql/firewall_create_user.sql Postgres function
scripts/apply-sql.ts Run raw SQL against DATABASE_URL
## How it works 1. Sign-ups emit `create:user` events with IP metadata. 2. `firewall_create_user(inet)` returns whether another sign-up from the same IP is allowed in a 5s window. 3. On abuse, recent users may have features cleared and a `firewall:block_users` event is recorded. ## Apply SQL after schema push ```bash pnpm db:push pnpm db:sql:firewall ``` For production, prefer `DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE` with a migration role when applying SQL.

O que é o @madda/app e como ele se compara a starters “tudo em um”.

O **@madda/app** é o CLI oficial da org [madda](https://www.npmjs.com/org/madda). Ele gera projetos [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) com a **madda stack** — foco em type-safety, DX e convenções que escalam. Inspirado no fluxo do [create-t3-app](https://create.t3.gg/), feito para o ecossistema madda. ## Não é um template gigante Não entregamos todas as bibliotecas possíveis. O CLI **compõe features** que você escolhe: - **Tailwind CSS** — estilo opcional - **ESLint + Prettier** — lint/format opcional - **Drizzle ORM** — opcional (`postgres` local ou `neon`) - **Better Auth** — só quando há banco - **Eventos + firewall** — rate-limit opcional com auth + banco Você recebe código real para evoluir — não um framework para “lutar”. ## O que vem no projeto
